exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Vector Given Its Coordinates Relative To a Given Basis

question.text: Find the vector $\mathbf{x}$, if $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \},$ and \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad [\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
We know that any vector in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \}$ has the form

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

where $x_1$ and $x_2$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,\mathcal{B}.$ Since we are told that $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix},$ we obtain

\begin{align*} \mathbf{x} &= \underbrace{(\,8\,)}_{x_1} \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + \underbrace{(\:-4\:)}_{x_2} \begin{bmatrix}9 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 32\\ -24 \\ -16 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -36 \\ 4 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -20 \\ -12 \end{bmatrix} . \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis by Inspection

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b_3}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1?$
question.explanation:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{\mathbf{x}} = \underbrace{(\:1\:)}_{x_1} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{\mathbf{b}_1} + \underbrace{(\:0\:)}_{x_2} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}}_{\mathbf{b}_2} + \underbrace{(\,-3\,)}_{x_3} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}}_{\mathbf{b}_3} \]

which means that

\[ \mathbf{x} = 1 \cdot \mathbf{b}_1 + 0 \cdot \mathbf{b}_2 + (-3) \cdot \mathbf{b}_3 \]

and therefore

\[ [\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \]

Finally, $x_1=1.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -10 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ 8 \\ -20 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -10 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ 8 \\ -20 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -3 & 10 \\ 4 & -10 & 8 \\ -2 & 6 & -20 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} M & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -3 & 10 \\ 4 & -10 & 8 \\ -2 & 6 & -20 \end{array} \right] & R_2& := R_2+(-4)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -3 & 10 \\ 0 & 2 & -32 \\ -2 & 6 & -20 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -3 & 10 \\ 0 & 2 & -32 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - 3x_2 = 10 \\ 2x_2 = -32. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =-16.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1-3(-16) = 10 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = -38. \]

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -38 \\ -16 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1 + x_2 = (-38) + (-16) = -54.$

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -10 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ -10 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -10 \\ 4 & 0 & 4 \end{array}\right]. \]

Now, we reduce $M$ using Gaussian elimination: \[ \begin{align} M &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -10 \\ 4 & 0 & 4 \end{array}\right] & R_2 & := R_2+(-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 \\ 4 & 0 & 4 \end{array}\right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-4)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & -12 & 24 \end{array}\right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-3)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 9 \end{array}\right] \end{align} \]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + 3x_2 = -5 \\ -4x_2 = 5\\ 0 = 9, \end{cases} \]

where the third equation is always false. Therefore, the system has no solution and we conclude that $\mathbf{x} \not\in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \}.$

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors

question.text:
Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \},$ where

\[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ -8 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ -4 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ -8 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ -4 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ -8 & 2 & -4 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} M & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ -8 & 2 & -4 \end{array} \right] & R_3& :=R_3+2R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 8 & 16 \end{array} \right] & R_3& :=R_3+4R_2\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 4 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 4x_1 + 3x_2 = 10 \\ -2x_2 = -4. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ 4x_1+3 \cdot 2 = 10 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 1. \]

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1 + x_2 = 1+2 = 3.$

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -9 \\ 7 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -9 \\ 7 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -3 & -9 \\ -1 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} M & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -3 & -9 \\ -1 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \end{array} \right] &R_1&\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 7 \\ 2 & -3 & -9 \end{array} \right] & R_1 & := R_1+R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 10\\ 2 & -3 & -9 \end{array} \right]& R_3 & := R_3-2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 10\\ 0 & -3 & -15 \end{array} \right]& R_3 & := R_3+\dfrac{3}{2}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 10\\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 3 \\ 2x_2 = 10. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =5.$

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1 + x_2 = 3 + 5 = 8.$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 4 & 2 \\ -5 & -2 & -4 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following: \begin{align*} M & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 4 & 2 \\ -5 & -2 & -4 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \end{array} \right] & R_2 & :=R_2+\dfrac{5}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \end{array} \right] & R_3 &: =R_3+(-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 0 & -8 & -1 \end{array} \right]& R_3 & := R_3+R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 2x_1 +4x_2 = 2 \\ 8x_2 = 1. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =\dfrac{1}{8}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ 2x_1+4\cdot \dfrac{1}{8} = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = \dfrac{3}{4}. \]

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{3}{4} \\[3pt] \dfrac{1}{8} \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1 + x_2 = \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{7}{8}.$

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_3=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ -15 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 +x_3 \mathbf{b}_3 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -2 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}&= \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ -15 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -15 \\ 4 & -2 & -4 & 6 \end{array} \right] & R_2 & :=R_2+2R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 & -4 & 6 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-4)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & -4 & -22 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-6)R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 & -16 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + x_2 = 7 \\ -x_2-2x_3 = -1 \\ 8x_3=-16. \end{cases} \]

From third equation we get $x_3=-2$ and substituting this value into the second equation yields $x_2 =-2(-2)+1=5. $ Finally, substituting $x_2=5$ into the first equation, we obtain \[ x_1+5 = 7 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 2. \] Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 5 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, \[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = 2+5+(-2) = 5. \]

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing More Than Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 +x_3 \mathbf{b}_3 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}&= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 & :=R_2+(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-1)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 3 \\ 0& -1 & 1 & 2 \end{array} \right] &R_2&\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0& -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 3 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+ (-3)R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0& -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + x_2 = -1 \\ - x_2 + x_3 = 2 \\ -x_3=-3. \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3=3.$ Substituting this into the second equation yields \[ -x_2+(3) = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 =1 . \] Finally, by substituting $x_2=1$ into the first equation we obtain
\[ x_1 +1 = -1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = -2. \]

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, \[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = (-2)+1+3 = 2. \]

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing More Than Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\2\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ 3\\-1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\0\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 1\\1 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 +x_3 \mathbf{b}_3 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\2\end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ 3\\-1\end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\0\end{bmatrix}&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 1\\1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 &-3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 1 & 1\\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-3)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 &-3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -5\\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_4 & := R_4+(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 &-3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -5\\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -3 \end{array} \right] & R_4 & := R_4+ (-1)R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 &-3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -5\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 +x_2 +x_3= 2 \\[3pt] \!\!\,\, -3x_2 - 2x_3 =1 \\[3pt] \qquad \, -2x_3 =-5 \\[3pt] \quad \qquad 0=-4, \end{cases} \]

where the fourth equation is always false. Therefore, the system has no solution and we conclude that \[\mathbf{x} \not\in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \}.\]

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing More Than Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 10 \\ -17 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 +x_3 \mathbf{b}_3 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}&= \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 10 \\ -17 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & 0 & 5 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 10 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & -17 \end{array} \right] & R_2 & :=R_2+2R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 20 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & -17 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+(-4)R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 20 \\ 0 & -10 & 3 & -37 \end{array} \right] & R_3 & := R_3+2R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 20 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 3 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + 2x_2 = 5 \\ 5x_2 = 20 \\ 3x_3=3. \end{cases} \]

From the second and third equations, we get $x_2=4$ and $x_3 =1$, respectively. Substituting $x_2=4$ into the first equation, we obtain \[ x_1+2(4) = 5 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = -3. \]

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, \[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = (-3)+4+1 = 2. \]

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing More Than Two Vectors

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{b}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then what is the value of $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{b}_1+x_2 \mathbf{b}_2 +x_3 \mathbf{b}_3 &= \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

\begin{align*} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 2 & 0 & 4 & 2\\ -2 & 2 & 3 & -5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 10 \end{array} \right] & R_2 & :=R_2+R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 2 & 0 & 4 & 2\\ 0 & 2 & 7 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 10 \end{array} \right] & R_1 & \leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -1 & 10\\ 0 & 2 & 7 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 2\\ \end{array} \right] & R_3 & :=R_3+(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -1 & 10\\ 0 & 2 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 & -18\\ \end{array} \right] & R_3 & :=R_3+ 3R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -1 & 10\\ 0 & 2 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 27 & -27\\ \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + 3x_2-x_3 = 10 \\ 2x_2+7x_3 = -3 \\ 27x_3=-27. \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation yields \[ 2x_2+7(-1) = -3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = 2. \]

Finally, by substituting $x_2= 2$ and $x_3=-1$ into the first equation we obtain \[ x_1 + 3(2)-(-1) = 10 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = 3. \]

Therefore, $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, \[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = 3+2+(-1) = 4. \]
